judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the header image inside the link to Rádio TJ Minas (the link's name comes from aria-label="Rádio TJ Minas"). The crop shows a microphone with radio waves and the words "radiotjminas", i.e. the Rádio TJ Minas logo; the alt "icone rede social radio tjmg" names that radio (TJMG = TJ Minas Gerais), so it does not describe something the image fails to show: the claim is false of the capture. The alt serves the image's purpose (identifying the link to the court's radio), and the link's aria-label already gives the destination; the "icone rede social" wording is verbose, not a 1.1.1 failure. The live HTML has the same alt, title and aria-label, so the capture does not differ. The model judged the visible logo wrongly.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the header search field; its placeholder "O que deseja encontrar?" is the only visible text prompting the field (the label "Busca global do Portal" is not visible in the screenshot). Screenshot pixels give #d1d1d1 on #ffffff, 1.53:1, and the live bundle.css sets ::placeholder {color:#d1d1d1}, at 14px normal weight, so 4.5:1 applies and the claim is true. Reasons it could pass were checked and do not hold: Understanding 1.4.3 says the criterion applies to placeholder text; the page's "Alto contraste" control (G174) loads /tjmg/rede/css/high-contrast.css, which returns 404 on the live site, and bundle.css has no high-contrast rules, so no conforming alternate presentation exists; the field is not disabled and the text is not incidental. The live CSS and HTML match the capture. The element fails 1.4.3 for the reason the claim names.

judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: The element is the icon-only "Compartilhar no Twitter" share link (fa-twitter glyph, name only in title) in the article header. The live bundle.css sets .share-article li.twitter a {color:#55acee} and the surrounding background measures #f7f7f7 in the screenshot, so 2.30:1 is true of the capture (in the full-page screenshot the fixed chatbot button happens to cover the icon, which does not change its colours). Whether it fails 1.4.11 is open: the glyph is the Twitter bird logo in Twitter's brand blue, and Understanding 1.4.11 says logos are exempted on the assumption that brand guidelines mandate their colours, only recommending a contrasting variant when a logo acts as a control; against that, the icon is the control's only visual identifier (G207), the page renders other share icons in #576180, and the bird and its blue are no longer a current brand requirement. Competent auditors would reasonably disagree on whether the logo exemption applies, so the label is uncertain.
